14:1.sourceText: Τὸν δὲ ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει προσλαμβάνεσθε, μὴ εἰς διακρίσεις διαλογισμῶν.
14:1.targetText: And receive him who is weak in the faith—not to determinations of reasonings;

14:2.sourceText: ὃς μὲν πιστεύει φαγεῖν πάντα, ὁ δὲ ἀσθενῶν λάχανα ἐσθίει.
14:2.targetText: one believes that he may eat all things—and he who is weak eats herbs;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek μέν marks the first half of the contrasted one/other construction; English expresses that contrast without a separate indeed.

14:3.sourceText: ὁ ἐσθίων τὸν μὴ ἐσθίοντα μὴ ἐξουθενείτω, ὁ δὲ μὴ ἐσθίων τὸν ἐσθίοντα μὴ κρινέτω, ὁ Θεὸς γὰρ αὐτὸν προσελάβετο.
14:3.targetText: do not let him who is eating despise him who is not eating: and do not let him who is not eating judge him who is eating, for God received him.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

14:4.sourceText: σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ κρίνων ἀλλότριον οἰκέτην; τῷ ἰδίῳ κυρίῳ στήκει ἢ πίπτει· σταθήσεται δέ, δυνατεῖ γὰρ ὁ Κύριος στῆσαι αὐτόν.
14:4.targetText: You—who are you that are judging another’s domestic [affairs]? To his own master he stands or falls; and he will be made to stand, for God is able to make him stand.

groups.note: Greek οἰκέτην is the personal household-servant noun, rendered domestic. The following bracketed affairs is an English supplement and is not treated as part of the Greek servant lexeme.

targetPhrases.text: he will be made to stand

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.
Source-witness divine-title difference: N1904 reads Κύριος, Lord, while LSV follows Θεός, God.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English noun supplied by LSV. The actual Greek οἰκέτην is a household servant or domestic, not a noun meaning affairs.
Source-witness divine-title difference: LSV follows Θεός while pinned N1904 reads Κύριος.

14:5.sourceText: ὃς μὲν γὰρ κρίνει ἡμέραν παρ’ ἡμέραν, ὃς δὲ κρίνει πᾶσαν ἡμέραν· ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ πληροφορείσθω.
14:5.targetText: One judges one day above another, and another judges every day [alike]; let each be fully assured in his own mind.

groups.note: The second Greek day noun is represented by the English pronominal another, whose day referent is understood; the later another refers instead to the other person judging.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.
Source-witness connective difference: N1904 has explanatory γάρ after the opening distributive words; LSV does not print that explanatory connective.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English comparison supplement supplied with every day.

14:6.sourceText: ὁ φρονῶν τὴν ἡμέραν Κυρίῳ φρονεῖ· καὶ ὁ ἐσθίων Κυρίῳ ἐσθίει, εὐχαριστεῖ γὰρ τῷ Θεῷ· καὶ ὁ μὴ ἐσθίων Κυρίῳ οὐκ ἐσθίει, καὶ εὐχαριστεῖ τῷ Θεῷ.
14:6.targetText: He who is regarding the day, he regards [it] to the LORD, and he who is not regarding the day, he does not regard [it] to the LORD. He who is eating, he eats to the LORD, for he gives thanks to God; and he who is not eating, he does not eat to the LORD, and gives thanks to God.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek καί introduces the eating clause; LSV begins that sentence directly after its additional day-disregard clause, without a separate conjunction for the eating clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English object supplied for regards; no separate Greek object pronoun is written at that point.

unmappedTarget.text: and he who is not regarding the day, he does not regard [it] to the LORD
unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: this whole additional non-observing-day clause follows the longer reading and is absent from pinned N1904.

14:7.sourceText: Οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἑαυτῷ ζῇ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἑαυτῷ ἀποθνῄσκει·
14:7.targetText: For none of us lives to himself, and none dies to himself;

14:8.sourceText: ἐάν τε γὰρ ζῶμεν, τῷ Κυρίῳ ζῶμεν, ἐάν τε ἀποθνήσκωμεν, τῷ Κυρίῳ ἀποθνήσκομεν. ἐάν τε οὖν ζῶμεν ἐάν τε ἀποθνήσκωμεν, τοῦ Κυρίου ἐσμέν.
14:8.targetText: for both, if we may live, we live to the LORD; if also we may die, we die to the LORD; both then if we may live, also if we may die, we are the LORD’s;

14:9.sourceText: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἔζησεν, ἵνα καὶ νεκρῶν καὶ ζώντων κυριεύσῃ.
14:9.targetText: for because of this Christ both died and rose again, and lived again, that He may be Lord both of dead and of living.

groups.note: The written ἔζησεν is lived or came to life; LSV makes the resurrection context explicit with lived again. No separate πάλιν word is asserted.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV follows the additional καί before died; pinned N1904 has no corresponding first additive particle.
Source-witness difference: LSV follows the additional resurrection clause καὶ ἀνέστη; pinned N1904 has died and lived, without that separate clause.

14:10.sourceText: Σὺ δὲ τί κρίνεις τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; ἢ καὶ σὺ τί ἐξουθενεῖς τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; πάντες γὰρ παραστησόμεθα τῷ βήματι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
14:10.targetText: And you, why do you judge your brother? Or again, you, why do you set at nothing your brother? For we will all stand at the judgment seat of the Christ;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.
Source-witness divine-name difference: N1904 has τοῦ Θεοῦ, of God, whereas LSV follows τοῦ Χριστοῦ, of the Christ.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness divine-name difference: LSV follows Christ, whereas pinned N1904 has God at this judgment-seat reference.

14:11.sourceText: γέγραπται γάρ Ζῶ ἐγώ, λέγει Κύριος, ὅτι ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ, καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσεται τῷ Θεῷ.
14:11.targetText: for it has been written: “I live! Says the LORD—Every knee will bow to Me, and every tongue will confess to God”;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces the declaration; English continues the quotation directly without a separate that.

14:12.sourceText: ἄρα οὖν ἕκαστος ἡμῶν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λόγον δώσει τῷ Θεῷ.
14:12.targetText: so, then, each of us will give reckoning to God concerning himself;

14:13.sourceText: Μηκέτι οὖν ἀλλήλους κρίνωμεν· ἀλλὰ τοῦτο κρίνατε μᾶλλον, τὸ μὴ τιθέναι πρόσκομμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἢ σκάνδαλον.
14:13.targetText: therefore, may we judge one another no longer, but rather judge this, not to put a stumbling-stone before the brother, or an offense.

groups.note: The dative brother names the person for whom the obstacle would be placed; English before the brother expresses that obstructing relation, not an independent Greek before preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article nominalizes the not-putting infinitive; English has no separate article.

14:14.sourceText: οἶδα καὶ πέπεισμαι ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ ὅτι οὐδὲν κοινὸν δι’ ἑαυτοῦ· εἰ μὴ τῷ λογιζομένῳ τι κοινὸν εἶναι, ἐκείνῳ κοινόν.
14:14.targetText: I have known, and am persuaded, in the Lord Jesus, that nothing [is] unclean of itself, except to him who is reckoning anything to be unclean—to that one [it is] unclean;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied after nothing.
Bracketed English subject and copula supplied in the final that-one-unclean nominal clause.

14:15.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ διὰ βρῶμα ὁ ἀδελφός σου λυπεῖται, οὐκέτι κατὰ ἀγάπην περιπατεῖς. μὴ τῷ βρώματί σου ἐκεῖνον ἀπόλλυε, ὑπὲρ οὗ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.
14:15.targetText: and if your brother is grieved through food, you no longer walk according to love; do not destroy with your food that one for whom Christ died.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.
Source-witness connective difference: N1904 reads γάρ, for, whereas LSV follows δέ, and.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: LSV follows δέ while pinned N1904 has the explanatory γάρ.

14:16.sourceText: μὴ βλασφημείσθω οὖν ὑμῶν τὸ ἀγαθόν.
14:16.targetText: Do not let, then, evil be spoken of your good,

groups.note: The passive blaspheming command is rendered by the English let-evil-be-spoken-of predicate. Evil is part of that lexical verb rendering, not an unrelated Greek evil adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

14:17.sourceText: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ βρῶσις καὶ πόσις, ἀλλὰ δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ χαρὰ ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ·
14:17.targetText: for the Kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit;

14:18.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ δουλεύων τῷ Χριστῷ εὐάρεστος τῷ Θεῷ καὶ δόκιμος τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
14:18.targetText: for he who in these things is serving the Christ, [is] acceptable to God and approved of men.

groups.note: The Greek dative men marks those by whom the service is approved; LSV uses of men in that evaluative-agent sense.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness pronoun-number difference: pinned N1904 has singular τούτῳ, D-DSN, this; LSV follows plural τούτοις, these things.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied before acceptable.
Source-witness pronoun-number difference: LSV follows plural τούτοις, while pinned N1904 writes singular τούτῳ, this.

14:19.sourceText: ἄρα οὖν τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης διώκομεν καὶ τὰ τῆς οἰκοδομῆς τῆς εἰς ἀλλήλους.
14:19.targetText: So, then, may we pursue the things of peace, and the things of building up one another.

groups.note: Pinned N1904 διώκομεν is present indicative V-PAI-1P, we pursue, while LSV follows the hortatory subjunctive διώκωμεν, may we pursue. The pursuing predicate and first-person plural subject are shared; the English may expresses the differing subjunctive mood, not a separate Greek permission word.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek attributive article links the following beneficiary-direction phrase to building up; no separate English article is written.
Greek εἰς marks the beneficiary relation toward one another; English building up directly takes one another as its object without a separate direction preposition.

14:20.sourceText: μὴ ἕνεκεν βρώματος κατάλυε τὸ ἔργον τοῦ Θεοῦ. πάντα μὲν καθαρά, ἀλλὰ κακὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ διὰ προσκόμματος ἐσθίοντι.
14:20.targetText: Do not cast down the work of God for the sake of food; all things, indeed, [are] pure, but evil [is] to the man who is eating through stumbling.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied in the all-things-pure nominal clause.
Bracketed English copula supplied in the evil-to-the-man clause.

14:21.sourceText: καλὸν τὸ μὴ φαγεῖν κρέα μηδὲ πιεῖν οἶνον μηδὲ ἐν ᾧ ὁ ἀδελφός σου προσκόπτει.
14:21.targetText: [It is] not right to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor to [do anything] in which your brother stumbles, or is made to fall, or is weak.

groups.note: The Greek wording is good not to eat; the displayed LSV places not with right in not right to eat. The good/right adjective is shared, while the English placement and scope of the negation differ.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article nominalizes the not-eating infinitive; no separate English article is written.

14:22.sourceText: σὺ πίστιν ἣν ἔχεις κατὰ σεαυτὸν ἔχε ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ. μακάριος ὁ μὴ κρίνων ἑαυτὸν ἐν ᾧ δοκιμάζει·
14:22.targetText: You have faith! Have [it] to yourself before God; blessed is he who is not judging himself in what he approves,

14:23.sourceText: ὁ δὲ διακρινόμενος ἐὰν φάγῃ κατακέκριται, ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως· πᾶν δὲ ὃ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἁμαρτία ἐστίν.
14:23.targetText: and he who is making a difference, if he may eat, has been condemned, because [it is] not of faith; and all that [is] not of faith is sin.
